key_insight: Disordered carbon materials exhibit glass-like thermal transport consistent with multiple activated coherence channels sharing approximately universal energy scales.
engineering_relevance: The proposed scaling framework could help model thermal conductivity across porous and disordered carbon materials with different densities and microstructures.
method: Measured thermal conductivity from 4.5 to 300 K in GO, reduced GO, GO–hydrated fullerene composites, expanded graphite, and graphite–MWCNT composites.
Compared a Peierls-plus-single-coherence model with a generalized model containing two or three Arrhenius-type coherence channels.
Examined activation-energy scaling and applied the framework to published disordered-carbon data.
evidence_signal: Across the measured materials, the single-coherence model systematically failed, while multichannel fits yielded E2 ≈ 4E1 and E3 ≈ 12–25E1, with amplitudes increasing with density and activation energies remaining nearly invariant.
watch_item: The model is phenomenological: agreement with conductivity data does not independently establish the microscopic origin or uniqueness of the inferred coherence channels.
paper_title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
